title: Contingency planning
headline: If 2020 repeated, CPN's own 51.6% core profit fall would cut FY2027E profit by ฿10.5bn, more than marketing can absorb, so credit is the constraint to watch.

top.trigger: Debt over 88% of GDP; 2027 growth forecast under 1.5%
top.response: Amber freezes, Red suspends lines; capped vouchers (R4)

top.trigger: Gen Z visits per active member below +5% at G3
top.response: Format zones (P1); move money to the best-performing format

top.trigger: Confirmed breach complaint or leak; no report in 72 hours
top.response: S1 set-up; aggregated extracts only; S4 survey ages 20+ only

worst.title: Worst cases and credit sensitivity
worst.text: TRIS Rating (AA+/Stable) flags sustained debt to EBITDA over 4 times. That is a sensitivity, not a limit. The ratio was 3.4 in 2025.

notes: The ratings are our judgement. Only household debt is rated high on both likelihood and impact. In our assessment, Gen Z disengagement is our biggest exposure. Our thesis rests on Gen Z, so gate three tests it. Our response is a three-step ladder. Amber freezes some spending. Red suspends lines and trims the flagship seasons by 20 percent. Crisis suspends most lines and runs tenant relief. A closure like 2020 would trigger Crisis. CPN's own core profit fell 51.6 percent then; the same fall on our base is 10.5 billion baht. Marketing cuts cannot absorb that, so credit is the constraint we watch.

facts.meaning: W3 pandemic-style closure, year 1: net profit down ฿10,542 million (51.6%) to ฿9,888 million; a team estimate that replays CPN's own 2020 and 2021 results on the FY2027E base case (net profit ฿20,430 million), before the ladder's offsets
facts.where: ch6.md Table 6.8 row W3, Impact on FY2027E and Basis; Table 6.8 title
facts.cite: team estimate; Central Pattana, 2021, pp. 161, 166; Central Pattana, 2022, pp. 169, 176

facts.meaning: W2 severe consumer recession: net profit down ฿4,812 million (23.6%) to ฿15,618 million on FY2027E

facts.on_slide: more than marketing cuts can absorb; credit is the constraint to watch (headline, notes)
facts.meaning: Marketing cuts cannot absorb the large cases: Crisis frees at most ฿1,545 million after 31 March against the ฿10,542 million loss in the 2020 replay; credit is the constraint to watch in the largest cases (team assessment)
facts.where: ch6.md 6.3 'Worst-case Risks' paragraph 2 and the paragraph after Table 6.8

facts.meaning: TRIS upgraded CPN to AA+/Stable on 26 February 2026

facts.on_slide: sustained debt to EBITDA over 4 times; a sensitivity, not a limit; the ratio was 3.4 in 2025
facts.meaning: Ratings could be revised downward if sustained debt to EBITDA exceeds 4 times; the ratio was 3.4 in 2025; the 4 times level is a sensitivity, not a limit

facts.on_slide: Worst cases and credit sensitivity (box title)
facts.meaning: The 4 times debt-to-EBITDA level is a TRIS sensitivity (ratings could be revised downward if it is sustained), not a limit; the box shows the closure and severe-recession worst cases and the team-calculated EBITDA headroom
facts.where: ch6.md 6.3 'Worst-case Risks' paragraph 2; Table 6.8 rows W2 and W3

facts.meaning: On TRIS's 2025 figures with debt unchanged, an EBITDA fall of about ฿4.6 billion (14%) would take the ratio to 4 times; headroom is a team calculation used as a yardstick

facts.on_slide: three-step ladder: Amber freezes some spending; Red suspends lines and trims the flagship seasons by 20 percent; Crisis suspends most lines and runs tenant relief (notes)
facts.meaning: Response ladder: Amber freezes lines 5 and 10 and holds new commitments on lines 4, 6, 9; Red adds suspension of lines 4, 6, 9 and trims lines 1 to 3 (the flagship windows, ch4 lines 1 to 3) by 20%; Crisis suspends lines 1 to 6, 9 and 10 and a standing crisis team runs tenant relief; lines 7, 8 and 11 are protected
facts.where: ch6.md Table 6.7, columns 'Budget action' and 'Reallocation'; Table 6.1 rows (lines 1 to 3)

facts.on_slide: a closure like 2020 would trigger our Crisis state and cut profit by more than half (notes)
facts.meaning: W3 pandemic-style closure: Crisis ladder from day one (entry rule: government closure order); year 1 profit down 51.6%, a team estimate
facts.where: ch6.md Table 6.8 row W3; Table 6.7 row Crisis

facts.on_slide: In our assessment, Gen Z disengagement is our biggest exposure (notes); gate three tests it
facts.meaning: The thesis is the largest exposure (team assessment); M1 supplies 47% of FY2028E uplift, so G3 tests Gen Z behaviour before the year-end season is released
facts.where: ch6.md 6.3 paragraph after Table 6.6; Table 6.2 row G3
